What has been the average annual rainfall in Pago Pago over the past 40 years?
ground_truth_chunks: The average annual rainfall in Pago Pago over the past 40 years has been about 508 cm (200 in).

records.question: Will the proposed dredging greatly increase the flushing rate of the lagoon?
records.ground_truth_answer: No. The measurements and analyses conclude the proposed dredging will not produce greatly increased flushing; the flushing rate might be slightly increased or possibly slightly decreased.
ground_truth_chunks: Offhand, it might be expected that deepening the entrance channel would greatly increase the flushing rate, but this will not be the case here.
The flushing rate might be slightly increased or possibly even slightly decreased by the proposed channel.

Although the problem is too complex to allow an exact prediction of which small change would occur, the measurements and analyses do lead firmly to the important overall conclusion: the proposed dredging will not produce greatly increased flushing of the lagoon.

records.question: Which regions of Pala Lagoon had the highest enteric bacterial densities during the survey?
records.ground_truth_answer: Enteric bacterial densities were highest in the northern and western regions of the lagoon, with the western and northwestern areas identified as zones of primary concern for fecal contamination.
ground_truth_chunks: Enteric bacterial densities were highest in the northern and western regions of the lagoon reflecting major source locations and circulatory patterns.
The present zones of primary concern are the western and northwestern areas of Pala Lagoon.
It is concluded from this study that, on the basis of enteric microbial density, the western and northwestern regions of Pala Lagoon show evidences of fecal contamination.

records.question: Which organisms dominated the surf zone on the fringing reef in front of Pala Lagoon (Transect A)?
records.ground_truth_answer: The coralline alga Porolithon sp. and the corals Acropora humilis and Pocillopora verrucosa dominated the surf zone.
ground_truth_chunks: The coralline alga, Porolithon sp., and the corals Acropora humilis and Pocillopora verrucosa were the dominant organisms in the surf zone.
Less common was the coral Millepora platyphylla.

records.question: How many total net samples were collected during the sampling period in Pala Lagoon?
records.ground_truth_answer: A total of 99 net samples was collected in 13 months of sampling.

records.question: What boat accommodation configuration did the Army Corps of Engineers initially propose for the Pala Lagoon small boat harbor?
records.ground_truth_answer: They proposed accommodation for 350 trailer-type craft, 10 pleasure boats of the inboard-outboard class, and 40 sailboats without auxiliary power.
ground_truth_chunks: The initial configuration of the Pala Lagoon small boat harbor proposed by the Army Corps of Engineers was based on the accommodation of 350 trailer-type craft, 10 pleasure boats of the inboard-outboard class, and 40 sailboats without auxiliary power.
The estimated cost of construction of a harbor to accommodate these crafts is \$1,490,000.

records.question: What is the maximum allowable median coliform bacteria concentration per 100 ml for Classes A, 1 & 2 waters?
records.ground_truth_answer: The median coliform bacteria shall not exceed 1,000 per 100 ml.
ground_truth_chunks: The median coliform bacteria shall not exceed 1,000 per 100 ml, nor shall more than 10 percent of the samples exceed 2,400 per 100 ml.

records.question: To what area does the Class B designation apply within bays and harbors?
records.ground_truth_answer: The Class B designation applies only to a limited area next to boat docking facilities in bays and harbors; the rest of the water area in such bay or harbor shall be Class A unless given some other specific designation in Section 5.
